theme.title: The 72–10 Bulls
theme.subtitle: Chicago, 1995–96
theme.recap: Chicago lost three games before February, won almost everywhere it played and finished with the best combined record in league history.

questions.prompt: Counting the regular season and playoffs together, how many games did the 1995–96 Bulls win?
questions.context: Chicago Bulls · 1995–96 · regular season plus playoffs
questions.note: 87 wins and 13 losses, the best combined record in NBA history.

source.name: Wikipedia contributors (CC BY-SA 4.0)
source.quote: The 1995–96 Bulls have the best combined regular and postseason record in NBA history at 87–13

funFacts.text: That Bulls team introduced black alternate road uniforms with red pinstripes, a look closely associated with the dynasty.

source.name: Wikipedia contributors (CC BY-SA 4.0)
source.quote: the Bulls revealed new black alternate road uniforms, which featured red pinstripes

funFacts.text: Chicago reunited several former Detroit Bad Boys teammates by adding Rodman, James Edwards and John Salley.

source.name: Wikipedia contributors (CC BY-SA 4.0)
source.quote: Rodman, Edwards and Salley were all teammates on the Detroit Pistons during the "Bad Boy" era

funFacts.text: The Bulls swept Orlando in the Eastern Conference finals, avenging the previous season's playoff elimination.

source.name: Wikipedia contributors (CC BY-SA 4.0)
source.quote: the Bulls swept the Magic to gain entry into the Finals

questions.prompt: How many rebounds per game did Dennis Rodman average for the 1995–96 Bulls?
questions.note: 14.9 a night, while scoring just 5.5 points.

source.name: Wikipedia contributors (CC BY-SA 4.0)
source.quote: Rodman averaged 5.5 points and 14.9 rebounds per game

funFacts.text: Rodman's scoring average was just 5.5 a night, illustrating how little his value depended on scoring points.

source.name: Wikipedia contributors (CC BY-SA 4.0)
source.quote: Rodman averaged 5.5 points and 14.9 rebounds per game

funFacts.text: Chicago acquired Rodman from the San Antonio Spurs in the offseason before its historic run.

source.name: Wikipedia contributors (CC BY-SA 4.0)
source.quote: the Bulls acquired controversial All-Star forward and rebound specialist Dennis Rodman from the San Antonio Spurs

funFacts.text: Rodman had already won four rebounding titles when he joined Chicago.

source.name: Wikipedia contributors (CC BY-SA 4.0)
source.quote: a nine-year veteran and four year rebounding champion

questions.prompt: Chicago opened 1995–96 with 37 straight home wins. How long did that home winning streak run in total?
questions.note: 44 in a row, then an NBA record.

source.name: Wikipedia contributors (CC BY-SA 4.0)
source.quote: The Bulls' started the regular season 37–0 at home, part of a then-NBA-record 44-game winning streak

funFacts.text: Chicago opened the regular season undefeated at home for its first 37 contests.

source.name: Wikipedia contributors (CC BY-SA 4.0)
source.quote: The Bulls' started the regular season 37–0 at home

funFacts.text: The team finished that regular season with a spectacular 39–2 record at the United Center.

source.name: Wikipedia contributors (CC BY-SA 4.0)
source.quote: the team also posted a league-best 39–2 home record at the United Center

funFacts.text: An 18-game winning streak over January and February contributed to Chicago's record-setting season.

source.name: Wikipedia contributors (CC BY-SA 4.0)
source.quote: The Bulls posted an 18-game winning streak between January and February

questions.prompt: How many road games did the 1995–96 Bulls win?
questions.note: 33, the most ever until the 2015–16 Warriors won 34.

source.name: Wikipedia contributors (CC BY-SA 4.0)
source.quote: Their 33 road wins were the most in NBA history until the 2015–16 Warriors won 34 road games.

funFacts.text: Golden State eventually surpassed Chicago's road-win mark during the 2015–16 campaign.

source.name: Wikipedia contributors (CC BY-SA 4.0)
source.quote: the 2015–16 Warriors won 34 road games

funFacts.text: The Bulls became the first team to exceed 70 regular-season wins and also take the championship.

source.name: Wikipedia contributors (CC BY-SA 4.0)
source.quote: the only team in NBA history to win more than 70 games and an NBA title in the same season

funFacts.text: Chicago entered the All-Star break with a 42–5 record after a blistering first half of the season.

source.name: Wikipedia contributors (CC BY-SA 4.0)
source.quote: held a 42–5 record at the All-Star break

questions.prompt: In Game 2 of the 1996 Finals, Dennis Rodman tied the Finals record for offensive rebounds. How many did he grab?
questions.note: 11 offensive rebounds, tying the Finals record.

source.name: Wikipedia contributors (CC BY-SA 4.0)
source.quote: Dennis Rodman tied an NBA Finals record with 11 offensive rebounds

funFacts.text: Michael Jordan earned Finals MVP for the fourth time as Chicago began a second three-title run.

source.name: Wikipedia contributors (CC BY-SA 4.0)
source.quote: Michael Jordan was named NBA Finals MVP, his fourth time winning the award

funFacts.text: Seattle reached the Finals behind Gary Payton and Shawn Kemp after defeating Utah in a seven-game Western final.

source.name: Wikipedia contributors (CC BY-SA 4.0)
source.quote: They then beat the Utah Jazz in seven games in the western finals

funFacts.text: The Bulls had fallen to Orlando a season earlier; in 1996 they swept the Magic on their way to the Finals.

source.name: Wikipedia contributors (CC BY-SA 4.0)
source.quote: the Bulls swept the Magic to gain entry into the Finals
